11197-bambi.title: Bambi
11197-bambi.creator: Marjorie Benton Cooke
11197-bambi.description: A book by Marjorie Benton Cooke. You almost said accomplishments! If you were not living in the Pliocene age, Professor James Parkhurst, you would know that accomplishments are a curse--accomplishment is the only thing that counts. I can sing a little, play the piano a little, auction bridge a good deal; I can cook, and sew fancy things. The only thing I can do well is to dance, and no real man wants to be supported by his wife's toes."

arxiv-1810-00980.title: A sampling framework for counting temporal motifs DOI: xx.xxx/xxx_x ISBN: xxx-xxxx-xx-xxx/xx/xx Conference: ACM WSDM conference; February 2019; Melbourne, Australia xxx-xxx-xx
arxiv-1810-00980.creator: Paul Liu, Austin R. Benson, Moses Charikar
arxiv-1810-00980.description: Abstract . Pattern counting in graphs is fundamental to network science tasks, and there are many scalable methods for approximating counts of small patterns, often called motifs, in large graphs. However, modern graph datasets now contain richer structure, and incorporating temporal information in particular has become a critical part of network analysis.

arxiv-1910-02503.title: Pomeron-pomeron scattering
arxiv-1910-02503.creator: István Szanyi, Volodymyr Svintozelskyi
arxiv-1910-02503.description: Abstract Central exclusive diffractive (CED) production of meson resonances potentially is a factory producing new particles, in particular a glueball. The produced resonances lie in trajectories with vacuum quantum numbers, essentially on the pomeron trajectory. A tower of resonance recurrences, the production cross section and the resonances widths are predicted.

arxiv-2102-03207.title: REAL-TIME DENOISING AND DEREVERBERATION WTIH TINY RECURRENT U-NET
arxiv-2102-03207.creator: Hyeong-Seok Choi, Sungjin Park, Jie Hwan Lee, Hoon Heo, Dongsuk Jeon, Kyogu Lee
arxiv-2102-03207.description: Abstract Modern deep learning-based models have seen outstanding performance improvement with speech enhancement tasks. The number of parameters of state-of-the-art models, however, is often too large to be deployed on devices for real-world applications. To this end, we propose Tiny Recurrent U-Net (TRU-Net), a lightweight online inference model that matches the performance of current state-of-the-art models.

arxiv-2112-09462.title: Contrastive Explanations for Comparing Preferences of Reinforcement Learning Agents
arxiv-2112-09462.creator: Jasmina Gajcin, Rahul Nair, Tejaswini Pedapati, Radu Marinescu, Elizabeth Daly, Ivana Dusparic
arxiv-2112-09462.description: Abstract In complex tasks where reward function is not straightforward and consists of a set of objectives, multiple reinforcement learning (RL) policies that perform task adequately, but employ different strategies can be trained by adjusting the impact of individual objectives on the reward function.

arxiv-2205-00127.title: Baba is You is Undecidable
arxiv-2205-00127.creator: Jonathan Geller
arxiv-2205-00127.description: Abstract We establish the undecidability of 2019 puzzle game Baba is You through a reduction from the Post correspondence problem. In particular, we consider a restricted form of the Post correspondence problem introduced by Neary (STACS 2015) that is limited to five pairs of words.

arxiv-2211-01747.title: Methodology for Simulation-based Comparison of Algorithms for Distributed Mutual Exclusion
arxiv-2211-01747.creator: Filip De Turck, Ghent University - imec, Belgium
arxiv-2211-01747.description: Abstract In this paper, we show how different types of distributed mutual algorithms can be compared in terms of performance through simulations. A simulation-based approach is presented, together with an overview of the relevant evaluation metrics and approach for statistical processing of the results.

arxiv-2307-05242.title: Relativistic Real-Time Methods Journal: Comprehensive Computational Chemistry
arxiv-2307-05242.creator: Marius Kadek, Lukas Konecny, Michal Repisky
arxiv-2307-05242.description: Abstract Recent advances in laser technology enable to follow electronic motion at its natural time-scale with ultrafast pulses, leading the way towards atto- and femtosecond spectroscopic experiments of unprecedented resolution. Understanding of these laser-driven processes, which almost inevitably involve non-linear light–matter interactions and non-equilibrium electron dynamics, is challenging and requires a common effort of theory and experiment.

arxiv-2502-06547.title: Data Augmentation and Regularization for Learning Group Equivariance
arxiv-2502-06547.creator: Oskar Nordenfors, Axel Flinth
arxiv-2502-06547.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Oskar Nordenfors, Axel Flinth. In many machine learning tasks, known symmetries can be used as an inductive bias to improve model performance. In this paper, we consider learning group equivariance through training with data augmentation. We summarize results from a previous paper of our own, and extend the results to show that equivariance of the trained model can be achieved through training on augmented data in tandem with regularization.

arxiv-2502-14786.title: SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features
arxiv-2502-14786.creator: Michael Tschannen, Alexey Gritsenko, Xiao Wang, Muhammad Ferjad Naeem, Ibrahim Alabdulmohsin, Nikhil Parthasarathy, Talfan Evans, Lucas Beyer, Ye Xia, Basil Mustafa, Olivier Hénaff, Jeremiah Harmsen, Andreas Steiner, Xiaohua Zhai
arxiv-2502-14786.description: Abstract We introduce SigLIP 2, a family of new multilingual vision-language encoders that build on the success of the original SigLIP. In this second iteration, we extend the original image-text training objective with several prior, independently developed techniques into a unified recipe—this includes captioning-based pretraining, self-supervised losses (self-distillation, masked prediction) and online data curation.

arxiv-2506-07092.title: Patient Similarity Computation for Clinical Decision Support: An Efficient Use of Data Transformation, Combining Static and Time Series Data
arxiv-2506-07092.creator: Joydeb Kumar Sana, Mohammad M. Masud, M Sohel Rahman, M Saifur Rahman
arxiv-2506-07092.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joydeb Kumar Sana, Mohammad M. Masud, M Sohel Rahman, M Saifur Rahman. Patient similarity computation (PSC) is a fundamental problem in healthcare informatics. The aim of the patient similarity computation is to measure the similarity among patients according to their historical clinical records, which helps to improve clinical decision support. This paper presents a novel distributed patient similarity computation (DPSC) technique based on data transformation (DT) methods, utilizing an effective combination of time series and static data.

arxiv-2508-08473.title: A Minimal Model for Emergent Collective Behaviors in Autonomous Robotic Multi-Agent Systems
arxiv-2508-08473.creator: Hossein B. Jond
arxiv-2508-08473.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hossein B. Jond. Collective behaviors such as swarming and flocking emerge from simple, decentralized interactions in biological systems. Existing models, such as Vicsek and Cucker-Smale, lack collision avoidance, whereas the Olfati-Saber model imposes rigid formations, limiting their applicability in swarm robotics. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a minimal yet expressive model that governs agent dynamics using relative positions, velocities, and local density, modulated by two tunable parameters: the spatial offset and kinetic offset.

arxiv-2601-07207.title: Thermodynamic Driving Force Activated Phonon Scattering in InN
arxiv-2601-07207.creator: Zaheer Ahmad, Osama A. Rana, Shakeel Ahmad, Mark Vernon, Brendan Cross, Alexander Kozhanov
arxiv-2601-07207.description: Abstract Defect related disorder during InN growth is a major challenge for making high performance electronic and optoelectronic devices. This is partly because film quality is often described using reactor specific settings instead of general physical variables. In this study, we show that plasma assisted MOCVD growth of InN can be described using a single thermodynamic driving force coordinate.

pmc-10717723.title: Dry suction versus wet suction technique of endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy for diagnosis of solid pancreatic lesions: study protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled non-inferiority trial
pmc-10717723.creator: Shenglin Xu, Junfen Wang, Jianian Guo, Fang Xie, Weiguang Qiao, Yiteng Meng, Peng Peng, Haiyan Hu, Ying Huang, Side Liu, Mengbin Qin, Jun Yao, Yue Li
pmc-10717723.description: BackgroundStudies have shown that the wet suction technique in endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) generates better histological diagnostic accuracy and specimen quality than the dry suction technique. However, conclusions of wet suction on the diagnostic accuracy of endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) are still controversial. Besides, the optimal number of passes for EUS-FNB has not been determined.

pmc-10735349.title: NOVEL MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN PLCG2, ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE, AND LONGEVITY
pmc-10735349.creator: Juan Palavicini, Juliet Garcia Rogers, Henry Miller, Susan Weintraub, Sarah Hopp
pmc-10735349.description: Phospholipase C-gamma-2 (PLCγ2) catalyzes the hydrolysis of the membrane phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) to form diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol trisphosphate (IP3), which subsequently feed into numerous downstream signaling pathways. PLCG2 rare coding variants are associated with both reduced (P522R) and increased (M28L) risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and with longevity (P522R).

pmc-11392268.title: Myosteatosis and the clinical outcomes of patients with liver cirrhosis: A meta-analysis
pmc-11392268.creator: Haojie Xue, Yihan Liu, Yang Liu, Han Li, Qian Liang, Longhui Ma, Junying Liu, Ming Zhao
pmc-11392268.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine the potential correlation between myosteatosis and the prognosis of patients diagnosed with liver cirrhosis by a meta-analysis.MethodsCohort studies of relevance were acquired through comprehensive searches of the Medline, Web of Science, and Embase databases. To account for heterogeneity, a random-effects model was employed to combine the findings.

pmc-12561850.title: Dyadic Coping and Communication as Predictors of 10-Year Relationship Satisfaction Subgroup Trajectories in Stable Romantic Couples
pmc-12561850.creator: Michelle Roth, Fridtjof W. Nussbeck, Selina A. Landolt, Mirjam Senn, Thomas N. Bradbury, Katharina Weitkamp, Guy Bodenmann
pmc-12561850.description: Given the importance of relationship satisfaction and the detrimental effects of its decline in romantic couples, it is crucial to understand how relationship satisfaction develops over time in long-term stable relationships and to identify predictors that explain such long-term changes.

pmc-12700916.title: GSK3 phosphorylates and activates trehalose-6-phosphate synthase to improve trehalose production and thermotolerance in Ganoderma lucidum
pmc-12700916.creator: Lingshuai Wang, Lingyan Shi, Hui Wang, Qiqi Han, Yuqing Hu, Qin Zheng, Zeyi Dong, Rui Liu, Mingwen Zhao, Huhui Chen
pmc-12700916.description: Glycogen synthase kinase 3 (GSK3) plays crucial roles in diverse organisms, yet its physiological functions in filamentous fungi remain poorly characterized. Here, we show that knockdown of GlGSK3 in Ganoderma lucidum leads to increased glycogen accumulation, reduced pyruvate and ATP production, and impaired hyphal growth and thermotolerance.

pmc-12774560.title: PNP as a Metabolic and Prognostic Driver of Breast Cancer Aggressiveness: Insights from Patient Tissue and Cell Models
pmc-12774560.creator: Sarra B. Shakartalla, Iman M. Talaat, Nival Ali, Shahenaz S. Salih, Zainab M. Al Shareef, Noura Alkhayyal, Riyad Bendardaf, Sameh S. M. Soliman
pmc-12774560.description: ObjectivesBreast cancer (BC) is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in women, largely due to metastasis. This study aims to explore the role of purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP), a key enzyme in purine metabolism, in the aggressiveness and metastatic behavior of BC.

pmc-12788545.title: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence-Based Diagnostic Tools for Accurate Detection and Classification of Oral Lesions: A Clinical Study
pmc-12788545.creator: Khushali Shah, Ankit Dhimole, Neetu Pandey, Robium Naorem, Rangoli Srivastava, Sameer Gupta
pmc-12788545.description: Background:Early detection and accurate classification of oral lesions are essential for effective clinical management and prevention of malignant transformation. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have led to the development of diagnostic tools aimed at enhancing clinical decision-making.Methods:A prospective clinical study was conducted involving 180 patients presenting with suspicious oral lesions at a tertiary dental care center.

pmc-13639363.title: Effectiveness of vedolizumab to reduce bowel urgency in a Canadian real-world inflammatory bowel disease cohort
pmc-13639363.creator: Parul Tandon, Yvette Leung, Ryan Ward, Abhinav Wadhwa, Jessica Weiss, Ruth Moulson, Christopher Pettengell, Robert Battat
pmc-13639363.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and AimsBowel urgency is a burdensome symptom of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that greatly impacts quality of life. This study evaluated vedolizumab effectiveness on bowel urgency in Canadian patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn’s disease (CD).MethodsAdults with moderately to severely active UC or CD with baseline Urgency Numeric Rating Scale (UNRS) scores enrolled in the Canadian Patient Support Program (July 2024–March 2025) were included. Bowel urgency and clinical endpoints were evaluated at 2, 6, and 14 weeks.

pmc-13674395.title: Bile acid metabolism and signaling in human and animal health: A One Health perspective
pmc-13674395.creator: Lei Li, Shuai Liu, Zhijun Cao, Yangchun Cao, Shengru Wu, Lu Deng, Junhu Yao, Jun Zhang
pmc-13674395.description: The One Health concept emphasizes the interdependence of human, animal, and ecosystem health. Against this broad backdrop, bile acids (BAs), as central products of host‐microbiota co‐metabolism, act far beyond their classical role in lipid emulsification. This review systematically summarizes BA biosynthesis, enterohepatic circulation, and gut microbiota‐mediated metabolic modification.

pmc-13680532.title: Introducing GABLE: Lightweight infrastructure for longitudinal experiments using Google Apps Script
pmc-13680532.creator: Ibrahim Berber, Ilke Kas, Tarun Sepuri, Brooke N. Macnamara, M. Cenk Çavuşoğlu, Amy L. Wilson-Delfosse, Elizabeth A. Krupinski, Philip J. Smith, Soumya Ray
pmc-13680532.description: Longitudinal studies are essential for understanding how behaviors, skills, and psychological states evolve over time. While online platforms have made study development easier, researchers still face major logistical challenges when managing multi-session studies, especially when coordinating large numbers of participants, session timing, reminders, and compensation.
